questions.q: What monitoring does `vm-catalog01` already have the moment it exists, before Theo configures anything?
options: None at all -- every metric requires manual setup
Platform metrics like Percentage CPU, Network In/Out, and Disk Read/Write Bytes, collected automatically with no agent or configuration
A fully built alert rule for CPU usage
A Log Analytics workspace, created automatically with the VM
questions.explain: Azure Monitor automatically collects platform metrics for most resources the moment they exist -- already more visibility than the on-prem server ever had.

questions.q: Why does Theo switch the CPU chart's aggregation from Average to Maximum before deciding whether the VM is undersized?
options: Average and Maximum always show identical results
Average can make a spiky CPU pattern look fine while Maximum reveals dangerous spikes the average hides
Maximum is required by Azure for all CPU metrics
Switching aggregation changes the VM's actual CPU usage
questions.explain: The same CPU data can look fine as an average while a real problem is hiding in the peaks -- switching to Maximum surfaces it.

questions.q: What does a Log Analytics workspace provide that platform metrics alone do not?
options: Nothing different -- they store identical data
A place to store and query detailed log data (with KQL), such as Activity Log records showing who made a specific change and when
Faster CPU performance for the VM
Automatic resizing of the VM when CPU is high
questions.explain: Metrics are numbers over time; logs are detailed event records that need a workspace to be queried, which is what lets a question like "who changed this?" get answered.

questions.q: In the alert rule "average CPU > 80% for 5 minutes," why does the 5-minute evaluation window matter?
options: It doesn't matter -- only the 80% threshold matters
Without it, a brief, completely normal CPU spike would trigger a noisy, useless alert; the window filters out momentary blips
5 minutes is the maximum window Azure allows
The window determines how often the VM is billed
questions.explain: The evaluation window is what separates a real sustained problem from a harmless two-second spike -- without it, alerting would be too noisy to trust.

questions.q: Why is the Action Group built as a separate, reusable object instead of being configured directly inside the alert rule?
options: Azure requires every alert to have its own unique Action Group
So the same notification setup (emailing Theo and Priya) can be attached to this alert and to future alerts, like a disk-space alert, without rebuilding it each time
Action Groups can only send SMS, never email
It has no real benefit -- it's just a historical naming convention
questions.explain: An Action Group is defined once and reused across as many alert rules as needed, so the whole team is notified consistently no matter which condition fired.
